purpose: Record adjacent public benchmark scopes, avoid claiming novelty for overlapping SRE/incident diagnosis, and define fair common-core integration targets. No benchmark score is asserted to be an OpsBench result.

benchmarks.title: ITBench: Evaluating AI Agents across Diverse Real-World IT Automation Tasks
limits: Initial paper results are tied to the paper's evaluated agents and benchmark release, not a 2026 general SOTA leaderboard.
Different tasks and agents must not be mixed into one headline rate.
An OpsBench synthetic result is not an ITBench result.
The code repository is pinned separately from the paper snapshot; public repository changes do not imply that the original paper's scores have been rerun.
benchmarks.next_step: Select eligible public SRE/CISO scenarios and implement an adapter/runner that preserves ITBench task identity, initial snapshots, evaluator and permissions; publish a separate common-core result.

benchmarks.title: ITBench-AA — Artificial Analysis independent ITBench SRE evaluation
benchmarks.publisher: Artificial Analysis, using IBM/ITBench public scenarios and additional private scenarios shared by ITBench authors

reported_scope.environment: offline Kubernetes incident snapshots containing alerts, events, traces, metrics and topology
reported_scope.primary_metric: average precision at full recall for root-cause entity attribution

limits: This is an incident diagnosis/root-cause entity attribution evaluation on offline snapshots, not live remediation or independently verified service restoration.
Its average-precision-at-full-recall metric is not the original ITBench paper's task-resolution percentage.
Private scenarios and three repeats are part of the evaluator's own implementation; do not infer access to private cases from the public GitHub repository.
benchmarks.next_step: Use the public 40-scenario-compatible subset as a diagnostic-only common-core candidate if the artifact/license/access terms permit; preserve AP@full-recall separately from OpsBench service outcome scores.

benchmarks.title: EnterpriseOps-Gym-AA — Artificial Analysis evaluation of ServiceNow EnterpriseOps-Gym
benchmarks.publisher: ServiceNow AI Research benchmark; independently evaluated by Artificial Analysis

reported_scope.environment: containerized, resettable enterprise simulation with live MCP servers
reported_scope.grading: strict task success; SQL verifiers inspect final database state; no partial credit

limits: The benchmark exercises multi-step enterprise workflows and final database-state verifiers, but a database-state pass is not by itself proof of external host/service health, safe operating-system effects or recovery.
ServiceNow authored the benchmark environment/dataset; Artificial Analysis independently implements and evaluates it. Neither is an independent audit of all product deployments.
The reported headline is an all-domain aggregate; compare only matching domain/task subsets with the same tool policy, dataset release, agent harness and repetitions.
benchmarks.next_step: Build a domain-scoped common-core adapter for ITSM and Hybrid tasks first; preserve the SQL verifier and task identities, then add separate independent service/host oracles only for OpsBench-owned remediation extensions.

benchmarks.title: A Better Benchmark Harness for SRE Agents

reported_scope.environment: Kubernetes microservice application with injected faults

reported_method.agent_comparison: PagerDuty SRE Agent, Claude Code and Codex configurations

limits: PagerDuty-authored benchmark report; not an independent vendor audit.
The reported sweep is one trial per agent; the report itself flags this statistical limitation.
The evaluated scope is diagnostic and recommendation quality; do not infer cross-customer SLA or enterprise service workflow performance.
benchmarks.next_step: Use its incident dimensions as a diagnostic subscore in matched experiments, while preserving OpsBench's independent postcondition and service-episode scoring.

benchmarks.title: AI SRE Arena
limits: The project explicitly states mitigation/readiness grade proposals, not executed repairs or verified recovery.
The published v1 uses one AI judge and reports no human-grader validation.
The published v1 does not measure time or cost.
The benchmark is product-authored and results reflect the published harness/configuration.
benchmarks.next_step: Pin the MIT Project Arena commit and reproduce a diagnosis-only common-core arm; separately extend selected cases with exact-plan approved repair, independent service health oracle and recovery verification.

benchmarks.title: RootCauseBench — Can AI find the commit that broke prod?

reported_scope.environment: frozen incident evidence and code/change context in Terminal-Bench/Harbor tasks

benchmarks.reported_method: The benchmark page reports 108 trials per fully evaluated model; top entries have reached the benchmark's 1.000 reward ceiling on that task set.
limits: It measures root-cause commit attribution, not execution of remediation or verified service restoration.
A saturated task set does not imply general SRE or IT operations are solved.
Commit attribution results should be used as a diagnostic/forensic sub-benchmark, not an OpsBench service-resolution score.
benchmarks.next_step: Use as an external diagnostic capability check for code/deploy-causality tasks; do not build a competing commit-attribution leaderboard inside OpsBench.

opsbench_nonduplicative_claim_surface: Customer service contract, SLA and escalation correctness across systems of record.
Exact authorization-to-effect binding across host, identity, ticket and connector operations.
Tenant isolation and secret handling across connector boundaries.
Ambiguous external responses, idempotency and no-blind-retry reconciliation.
Executed remediation with independent postcondition and recovery verification.
Truthful resolved, mitigated, escalated, safe-refusal and indeterminate outcomes.
Operator effort, elapsed time, rework, customer effort and total cost per verified resolution.
